nodes.summary: Every separable real Banach space $E$ admits a linear isometric embedding $e \colon E \to C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ into the space of continuous real functions on $[0, 1]$ with the supremum norm, such that the range of $e$ is closed.
nodes.title: Banach–Mazur embedding theorem

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a uniformly convex real Banach space and let $(x_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $E$. Then there are a strictly increasing map $\varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a point $y \in E$ such that the Cesàro means $\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_{\varphi(i)}$ converge to $y$ in norm as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Banach–Saks theorem for uniformly convex spaces

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Hausdorff spaces, and let $C(X, \mathbb{R})$ and $C(Y, \mathbb{R})$ be the real Banach spaces of continuous real functions on them with the supremum norm. If there is a surjective linear isometry from $C(X, \mathbb{R})$ onto $C(Y, \mathbb{R})$, then $X$ and $Y$ are homeomorphic.
nodes.title: Banach–Stone theorem for real scalars

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with dual space $E^*$. The functionals that attain their norm on the closed unit ball, that is, the $f \in E^*$ such that $|f(x)| = \|f\|$ for some $x \in E$ with $\|x\| \le 1$, form a dense subset of $E^*$ in the norm topology.
nodes.title: Bishop–Phelps theorem

nodes.summary: Let $C[0,1]$ be the real Banach space of continuous functions $[0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ with the supremum norm, and let $I$ be the identity operator on it. Every compact bounded linear operator $T : C[0,1] \to C[0,1]$ satisfies $\|I + T\| = 1 + \|T\|$, where the norms are operator norms.
nodes.title: Daugavet's theorem for compact operators

nodes.summary: Every infinite-dimensional real Banach space $E$ contains a series that converges unconditionally but not absolutely: there is a sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in $E$ such that the rearranged series $\sum_n x_{\sigma(n)}$ converges for every permutation $\sigma$ of $\mathbb{N}$, while $\sum_n \lVert x_n \rVert$ diverges.
nodes.title: Dvoretzky–Rogers theorem

nodes.summary: There is a constant $K > 0$ such that for all $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, every real $m \times n$ matrix $A = (a_{ij})$, every real Hilbert space $H$ and all vectors $x_1, \dots, x_m, y_1, \dots, y_n \in H$ of norm at most $1$, there are signs $\varepsilon_1, \dots, \varepsilon_m, \delta_1, \dots, \delta_n \in \{1, -1\}$ such that…
nodes.title: Grothendieck's inequality (real case)
Injections of a unit sphere into the unit interval

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a uniformly convex Banach space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $E^*$ be the space of continuous linear functionals on $E$. Then every continuous linear functional $\Phi$ on $E^*$ is evaluation at a point: there is $x \in E$ with $\Phi(f) = f(x)$ for every $f \in E^*$.
nodes.title: Milman–Pettis theorem
Normed spaces isometric to their duals

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
